requirements.evidence: Migrations match the spec: entities slug unique 'entities_slug_unique', softDeletes (create_entities_table.php:16-19); memberships FKs cascadeOnDelete, role default 'employee', storedAs owner_seq "case when role = 'owner' then 1 else null end", unique indexes with the required names (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-28). Contract is complete: Entity getRouteKeyName/memberships/users/owner() = hasOne(...)->owner() (Entity.php:23-58), EntityMembership cast + #[Scope] owner/admin/employee + relations, UserRole::manageable(), User::memberships/entities/membershipFor, factories with states. Policies implement the rules, but EntityMembershipPolicy::assignRole adds a restriction the task does not state ('if ($membership->role === UserRole::Owner) return false;', EntityMembershipPolicy.php:27-29), so the owner cannot assignRole on the owner membership even though the task says owner/admin may assign roles.

conventions.evidence: Authorization lives in app/Policies with auto-discovery tested (EntityPolicyTest.php:63-68). Migrations have timestamped generator-style names and reversible down() (create_entity_memberships_table.php:35-38). $fillable is deliberate via #[Fillable(['entity_id','user_id','role'])], which leaves the generated owner_seq out (EntityMembership.php:13). Docs updated: database-schema.md drops owner_membership_id and documents owner_seq and the index names; business-rules.md and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] updated. Style matches User.php (#[Fillable], casts(), PHPDoc on public methods).

security.evidence: Non-members resolve to a null role and are denied everywhere (EntityPolicy.php:62-65, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:63-66). Cross-entity admins are denied (tests at EntityPolicyTest.php:52-61, EntityMembershipPolicyTest.php:55-60). The owner membership can never be deleted. The DB enforces at most one owner. Mass assignment is limited by #[Fillable]. Small nit: the strict 'user_id === getKey()' comparison (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:46) relies on integer hydration.

tests.evidence: Five Pest files cover the schema: index names and columns, default role, duplicate membership, second-owner rejection, separate owners per entity, many non-owners, cascades and soft-deleted slugs (EntitySchemaTest.php). Model tests cover the factory, the cast, the scopes, the relations, owner() null/eager loading, membershipFor and mass assignment of owner_seq (EntityModelTest.php, EntityMembershipModelTest.php). Policy tests cover every role, non-members, other-entity members, self-removal, owner-membership protection and Gate discovery.

simplicity.evidence: Each policy has two small private helpers (roleIn, canManage) and no extra layers. owner() reuses the local scope via hasOne(...)->owner(). Only one shared test helper, memberWith(), was added (tests/Pest.php:58-61).

readability.evidence: Clear names and short methods. PHPDoc explains the intent behind non-obvious choices: the migration comment on NULLs in unique indexes (create_entity_memberships_table.php:21-22) and the assignRole note on owner transfer (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:22-24). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Only models, enum, policies, factories, migrations, tests, the requested doc updates and the CHANGELOG were changed. No routes, session, middleware, pages or translations, all of which are out of scope.

issues.explanation: assignRole always denies when the target is the owner membership, a rule the task does not specify ('owner and admin may assign roles'). It is reasonable and documented, but it goes beyond the contract and could disagree with the intended behaviour.

Self-removal uses a strict '$membership->user_id === $user->getKey()' comparison. If a driver hydrates the FK as a string, self-removal would be denied; casting or using $membership->user()->is($user) would be more robust.

review.summary: The change adds the entities and entity_memberships migrations, including a portable owner_seq generated column with a unique index that enforces one owner per entity. It also adds the Entity, EntityMembership and UserRole models, the factories, both policies, thorough Pest tests and the required doc and CHANGELOG updates, all within scope. The only notable deviation is an extra rule in assignRole that denies role assignment on the owner membership; it is a defensible choice that the task did not ask for, so I would approve with nits.
